verses.gurmukhi: ਅੰਬਰੀਕ ਮੁਹਿ ਵਰਤੁ ਹੈ ਰਾਤਿ ਪਈ ਦੁਰਬਾਸਾ ਆਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: a(n)bareek muh varat hai raat piee dhurabaasaa aaiaa|

en.bdb: One evening while king Ambaris was fasting he was visited by sage Durvasa

verses.gurmukhi: ਭੀੜਾ ਓਸੁ ਉਪਾਰਣਾ ਓਹੁ ਉਠਿ ਨ੍ਹਾਵਣਿ ਨਦੀ ਸਿਧਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: bheeRaa os upaaranaa oh uTh nhaavan nadhee sidhaiaa|

en.bdb: The king was to break his fast while serving Durvasa but the rishi went to the riverbank to take a bath.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਰਣੋਦਕੁ ਲੈ ਪੋਖਿਆ ਓਹੁ ਸਰਾਪੁ ਦੇਣ ਨੋ ਧਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: charanodhak lai pokhiaa oh saraap dhen no dhaiaa|

en.bdb: Fearing the change of date (which would deem his fast fruitless), the king broke his fast by drinking the water which he had poured on the feet of the rishi. When the rishi realised that the king had not served him first, he ran to curse the king.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਕ੍ਰ ਸੁਦਰਸਨੁ ਕਾਲ ਰੂਪ ਹੋਇ ਭੀਹਾਵਲੁ ਗਰਬੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: chakr sudharasan kaal roop hoi bheehaaval garab gavaiaa|

en.bdb: On this, Vishnu ordered his death like disc to move towards Durvasa  and thus the ego of Durvasa was removed.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਾਮ੍ਹਣੁ ਭੰਨਾ ਜੀਉ ਲੈ ਰਖਿ ਨ ਹੰਘਨਿ ਦੇਵ ਸਬਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: baamhan bha(n)naa jeeau lai rakh na ha(n)ghan dhev sabaiaa|

en.bdb: Now Brahmin Durvasa ran for his life. Even the gods and deities could not afford him shelter.

verses.gurmukhi: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ੍ਰ ਲੋਕੁ ਸਿਵ ਲੋਕੁ ਤਜਿ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਲੋਕੁ ਬੈਕੁੰਠ ਤਜਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: ei(n)dhrr lok siv lok taj braham lok baiku(n)Th tajaiaa|

en.bdb: He was avoided in the abodes of Indra, Siva, Brahma and the heavens.

verses.gurmukhi: ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਭਗਵਾਨੁ ਸਣੁ ਸਿਖਿ ਦੇਇ ਸਭਨਾਂ ਸਮਝਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: dhevatiaa(n) bhagavaan san sikh dhei sabhanaa(n) samajhaiaa|

en.bdb: Gods and God made him understand (that none except Ambaris could save him).

verses.gurmukhi: ਆਇ ਪਇਆ ਸਰਣਾਗਤੀ ਮਾਰੀਦਾ ਅੰਬਰੀਕ ਛੁਡਾਇਆ।
verses.translit_en: aai piaa saranaagatee maareedhaa a(n)bareek chhuddaiaa|

en.bdb: Then he surrendered before Ambaris and Ambaris saved the dying sage.
The Lord God came to be known in the world as benevolent to devotees.
